findings.title: Ref-count over-release
findings.body:
One `inheritedHandleRefsAdded` bool tracks the ref-count for every handle in the list. It becomes true after the first successful `DangerousAddRef`. If a later handle is disposed (so `DangerousAddRef` throws) or is null (NullReferenceException), the `finally` block calls `DangerousRelease` on every entry in `inheritedHandles`. That includes handles that were never AddRef'd and null entries.

The result is an unbalanced release, which can close a caller's still-in-use SafeHandle early, or a NullReferenceException in `finally`. Track how many refs were actually added (or keep a per-handle flag) and release only those.

findings.title: Lock leak in finally
Concurrent start race
findings.body:
Starts that set `InheritedHandles` now take only a read lock, so they run concurrently. Suppose two such starts list the same `SafeHandle`, e.g. a shared log pipe. When the first finishes, `CleanupHandles` clears `HANDLE_FLAG_INHERIT` while the second may be about to call `CreateProcess`. `PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST` requires every listed handle to be inheritable, so the second start fails intermittently with ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER.

Possible fixes: reference-count inherit-flag changes per handle, or serialize these starts.

Ref-count over-release
One `inheritedHandleRefsAdded` bool tracks the ref-count for every handle in the list. It becomes true after the first successful `DangerousAddRef`. If a later handle is disposed (so `DangerousAddRef` throws) or is null (NullReferenceException), the `finally` block calls `DangerousRelease` on every entry in `inheritedHandles`. That includes handles that were never AddRef'd and null entries. The result is an unbalanced release, which can close a caller's still-in-use SafeHandle early, or a NullReferenceException in `finally`. Track how many refs were actually added (or keep a per-handle flag) and release only those. Lock leak in finally
`CleanupHandles` runs inside `finally`, before `ExitReadLock`/`ExitWriteLock`, and it can throw a `Win32Exception`. It can also throw `ObjectDisposedException` from SafeHandle marshaling, because `DangerousRelease` runs before `SetHandleInformation(safeHandle, ...)` and may drop the last ref. If it throws: - the remaining handles are never released or un-inherited; - the original exception is masked; - `s_processStartLock` is never exited, so every later `Process.Start` deadlocks. Fix: clear the inherit flag before releasing, avoid throwing from cleanup, and exit the lock in its own `finally`. Concurrent start race
Starts that set `InheritedHandles` now take only a read lock, so they run concurrently. Suppose two such starts list the same `SafeHandle`, e.g. a shared log pipe. When the first finishes, `CleanupHandles` clears `HANDLE_FLAG_INHERIT` while the second may be about to call `CreateProcess`. `PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST` requires every listed handle to be inheritable, so the second start fails intermittently with ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER. Possible fixes: reference-count inherit-flag changes per handle, or serialize these starts.
